**Finding: compliant (at fallback) — no redline proposed.**

Section 12.3 gives us, AbbVie, a broad termination-for-convenience right ("for any or no reason") on 90 days' written notice, exercisable in the entirety or on a country-by-country basis, with no early-termination fee or break payment anywhere in Article 12. Harpoon has no convenience right — its exits are limited to material breach (12.2.1), Major Market diligence breach (12.2.2, scoped to that market only) and insolvency (12.4), all mutual and cure-protected.

That combination lands squarely within the playbook fallback (customer termination on 60–90 days' notice, no fee, no vendor convenience right), so it is acceptable and not redlined. Two points noted in the rationale but not flagged: notice is 90 days rather than the preferred 30; and termination under 12.3 triggers reversion of the Licensed Compounds/Products (12.6.1, 12.7) plus a sell-off period whose length Harpoon sets in its sole discretion (12.10.2) — ordinary reversion mechanics for a development/option licence rather than a penalty on our exit. The pro-rata prepaid-fee refund mechanic is inapplicable to this milestone/royalty structure.
